title: DevOps Agents That Can’t Delete Your Database | George Fahmy, Stakpak
description:
This is a teaser for George Fahmy’s full session at AI Native DevCon Fall, Nov 18–19.

You’ve seen the horror stories — AI coding agents deleting databases or wiping entire codebases. Why do existing safeguards like Claude Code’s whitelists and blacklists fail? Because LLMs are versatile — they can cause the same damage in a hundred different ways.

In this live demo, George Fahmy (Founder & CEO, Stakpak) introduces Warden, a new deterministic security enforcer that creates true boundaries agents can’t cross — no matter what tool or model they use. You’ll see how deterministic guardrails, secure secret handling, and mTLS for MCP can make coding agents safe for production use.

In the full DevCon talk, you’ll learn:
- Why traditional agent safety measures don’t work
- How deterministic security guardrails protect your infrastructure
- Practical examples from Stakpak’s open-source DevOps agent
- A Rust-based reference implementation for production-safe agents

About the speaker:
George Fahmy is the Founder & CEO of Stakpak, an open-source startup building AI agents that make DevOps suck less. Previously a founding engineer at Thndr (YC S20) and deep-tech crypto startup Liquidity Network, George has published academic work in distributed systems and is obsessed with security, GenAI, and improving developer experience.
